outcomeNote: An aggadic anthology: no question is posed and nothing is refuted. The only argumentative motion is internal to the Sages of Yavne's maxim, where a floated objection is knocked down by a taught ruling.

segments.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בָּתַר דִּמְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ, שֶׁתְּשַׁכֵּן בְּפוּרֵינוּ אַהֲבָה וְאַחְוָה וְשָׁלוֹם וְרֵיעוּת. וְתַרְבֶּה גְּבוּלֵנוּ בְּתַלְמִידִים וְתַצְלִיחַ סוֹפֵנוּ אַחֲרִית וְתִקְוָה. וְתָשִׂים חֶלְקֵנוּ בְּגַן עֵדֶן, וְתַקְּנֵנוּ בְּחָבֵר טוֹב וְיֵצֶר טוֹב בְּעוֹלָמֶךָ. וְנַשְׁכִּים וְנִמְצָא יִחוּל לְבָבֵנוּ לְיִרְאָה אֶת שְׁמֶךָ, וְתָבֹא לְפָנֶיךָ קוֹרַת נַפְשֵׁנוּ לְטוֹבָה״.
segments.en: The Gemara describes how «after Rabbi Elazar concluded his prayer, he said the following» additional prayer: «May it be Your will, Lord our God,» «to cause to dwell in our lot love and brotherhood, peace and friendship.» «And may You make our borders rich in disciples» «and cause us to ultimately succeed,» that we will have a good «end and hope.» «And may You set our portion in the Garden of Eden,» «and may You establish for us a good companion and a good inclination in Your world.» «And may we rise early and find the aspiration of our hearts to fear Your name,» «and may the satisfaction of our souls come before You,» i.e., may You hear our prayers that we may have spiritual contentment in this world «for the best.»

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בָּתַר דִּמְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ, שֶׁתָּצִיץ בְּבׇשְׁתֵּנוּ, וְתַבִּיט בְּרָעָתֵנוּ, וְתִתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּרַחֲמֶיךָ, וְתִתְכַּסֶּה בְּעֻזֶּךָ, וְתִתְעַטֵּף בַּחֲסִידוּתֶךָ, וְתִתְאַזֵּר בַּחֲנִינוּתֶךָ, וְתָבֹא לְפָנֶיךָ מִדַּת טוּבְךָ וְעִנְוְתָנוּתֶךְ״.
segments.en: Similarly, the Gemara recounts that «after Rabbi Yoḥanan concluded his prayer, he said the following» additional prayer: «May it be Your will, Lord our God,» «that You look upon our shame and behold our plight,» «that You clothe Yourself in Your mercy,» «and cover Yourself with Your might,» «that You wrap Yourself in Your loving-kindness,» «and gird Yourself with Your grace,» «and may Your attributes of goodness and humility come before You.»

segments.he: רַבִּי זֵירָא בָּתַר דִּמְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ, שֶׁלֹּא נֶחֱטָא וְלֹא נֵבוֹשׁ וְלֹא נִכָּלֵם מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ״.
segments.en: Similarly, «after Rabbi Zeira concluded his prayers he said the following» additional prayer: «May it be Your will, Lord our God,» «that we not sin or shame ourselves,» «and that we not disgrace ourselves before our forefathers,» in the sense that our actions should not disgrace the actions of our forefathers.

segments.he: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ, שֶׁתְּהֵא תּוֹרָתְךָ אוּמָּנוּתֵנוּ, וְאַל יִדְוֶה לִבֵּנוּ, וְאַל יֶחְשְׁכוּ עֵינֵינוּ״.
segments.en: «After Rabbi Ḥiyya prayed he said the following:» «May it be Your will, Lord our God,» «that Your Torah should be our vocation,» «and may our heart not become faint nor our eyes dim.»

segments.he: רַב בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ שֶׁתִּתֵּן לָנוּ חַיִּים אֲרוּכִּים, חַיִּים שֶׁל שָׁלוֹם, חַיִּים שֶׁל טוֹבָה, חַיִּים שֶׁל בְּרָכָה, חַיִּים שֶׁל פַּרְנָסָה, חַיִּים שֶׁל חִלּוּץ עֲצָמוֹת, חַיִּים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם יִרְאַת חֵטְא, חַיִּים שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם בּוּשָׁה וּכְלִימָּה, חַיִּים שֶׁל עוֹשֶׁר וְכָבוֹד, חַיִּים שֶׁתְּהֵא בָּנוּ אַהֲבַת תּוֹרָה וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם, חַיִּים שֶׁתְּמַלֵּא לָנוּ אֶת כָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבֵּנוּ לְטוֹבָה״.
segments.en: «After his prayer, Rav said the following:» «May it be Your will, Lord our God,» «that You grant us long life, a life of peace,» «a life of goodness, a life of blessing,» «a life of sustenance, a life of freedom of movement» from place to place, where we are not tied to one place, «a life of dread of sin, a life without shame and disgrace,» «a life of wealth and honor,» «a life in which we have love of Torah and reverence for Heaven,» «a life in which You fulfill all the desires of our heart for good.»

segments.he: רַבִּי בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ, שֶׁתַּצִּילֵנוּ מֵעַזֵּי פָּנִים וּמֵעַזּוּת פָּנִים, מֵאָדָם רָע, וּמִפֶּגַע רָע, מִיֵּצֶר רָע, מֵחָבֵר רָע, מִשָּׁכֵן רָע, וּמִשָּׂטָן הַמַּשְׁחִית, וּמִדִּין קָשֶׁה וּמִבַּעַל דִּין קָשֶׁה, בֵּין שֶׁהוּא בֶּן בְּרִית בֵּין שֶׁאֵינוֹ בֶּן בְּרִית״.
segments.en: «After his prayer, Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «said the following:» «May it be Your will, Lord our God, and God of our forefathers,» «that You save us from the arrogant and from arrogance» in general, «from a bad man, from a bad mishap,» «from an evil instinct, from a bad companion,» «from a bad neighbor, from the destructive Satan,» «from a harsh trial and from a harsh opponent,» «whether he is a member of the covenant,» a Jew, «or whether he is not a member of the covenant.»

segments.he: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקָיְימִי קָצוֹצֵי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי.
segments.en: «And» the Gemara notes that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi would recite this prayer every day «despite the fact that» royal «officers stood» watch «over Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi for his protection; nevertheless, he prayed to avoid conflict or hindrance resulting from arrogance.

segments.he: רַב סָפְרָא בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ, שֶׁתָּשִׂים שָׁלוֹם
segments.en: «After his prayer, Rav Safra said the following:» «May it be Your will, Lord our God, that You establish peace»

segments.he: בְּפָמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה. וּבְפָמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַטָּה, וּבֵין הַתַּלְמִידִים הָעוֹסְקִים בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ בֵּין עוֹסְקִין לִשְׁמָהּ בֵּין עוֹסְקִין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ. וְכָל הָעוֹסְקִין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁיְּהוּ עוֹסְקִין לִשְׁמָהּ״.
segments.en: «in the heavenly entourage [pamalia]» of angels each of whom ministers to a specific nation (see Daniel 10), and whose infighting causes war on earth; «and in the earthly entourage,» the Sages, «and among the disciples engaged in» the study of «Your Torah,» «whether they engage in its» study «for its own sake or not for its own sake.» «And all those engaged» in Torah study «not for its own sake,» «may it be» Your «will» that «they will come to engage» in its study «for its own sake.»

segments.he: רַבִּי אָלֶכְּסַנְדְרִי בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי: ״יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ, שֶׁתַּעֲמִידֵנוּ בְּקֶרֶן אוֹרָה, וְאַל תַּעֲמִידֵנוּ בְּקֶרֶן חֲשֵׁכָה, וְאַל יִדְוֶה לִבֵּנוּ, וְאַל יֶחְשְׁכוּ עֵינֵינוּ״. אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, הָא רַב הַמְנוּנָא מְצַלֵּי לַהּ. וְרַבִּי אָלֶכְּסַנְדְרִי בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי: ״רִבּוֹן הָעוֹלָמִים, גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנֶיךָ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנֶךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב? — שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיוֹת. יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ שֶׁתַּצִּילֵנוּ מִיָּדָם, וְנָשׁוּב לַעֲשׂוֹת חוּקֵּי רְצוֹנְךָ בְּלֵבָב שָׁלֵם״.
segments.en: «After his prayer, Rabbi Alexandri said the following:» «May it be Your will, Lord our God,» «that You station us in a lighted corner and not in a darkened corner,» «and do not let our hearts become faint nor our eyes dim.» «Some say that this was the prayer that Rav Hamnuna would recite, and that after Rabbi Alexandri prayed, he would say the following:» «Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You» «that our will is to perform Your will, and what prevents us?» On the one hand, «the yeast in the dough,» the evil inclination that is within every person; «and the subjugation to the kingdoms» on the other. «May it be Your will» «that You will deliver us from their hands,» of both the evil inclination and the foreign kingdoms, so that «we may return to perform the edicts of Your will with a perfect heart.»

segments.he: רָבָא בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי: ״אֱלֹהַי, עַד שֶׁלֹּא נוֹצַרְתִּי אֵינִי כְּדַאי, וְעַכְשָׁיו שֶׁנּוֹצַרְתִּי כְּאִלּוּ לֹא נוֹצַרְתִּי. עָפָר אֲנִי בְּחַיַּי, קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּמִיתָתִי, הֲרֵי אֲנִי לְפָנֶיךָ כִּכְלִי מָלֵא בּוּשָׁה וּכְלִימָּה. יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהַי, שֶׁלֹּא אֶחֱטָא עוֹד, וּמַה שֶּׁחָטָאתִי לְפָנֶיךָ מָרֵק בְּרַחֲמֶיךָ הָרַבִּים, אֲבָל לֹא עַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִין וָחֳלָאִים רָעִים״. וְהַיְינוּ וִידּוּי דְרַב הַמְנוּנָא זוּטֵי בְּיוֹמָא דְכִפּוּרֵי.
segments.en: «After his prayer, Rava said the following:» «My God, before I was created I was worthless,» «and now that I have been created it is as if I had not been created,» I am no more significant. «I am dust in life, all the more so in my death.» «I am before You as a vessel filled with shame and humiliation.» Therefore, «may it be Your will, Lord my God, that I will sin no more,» «and that those» transgressions «that I have committed,» «cleanse in Your abundant mercy;» «but» may this cleansing «not» be «by means of suffering and serious illness,» but rather in a manner I will be able to easily endure. «And this is the confession of Rav Hamnuna Zuti on Yom Kippur.»

segments.he: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא כִּי הֲוָה מְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי: ״אֱלֹהַי, נְצוֹר לְשׁוֹנִי מֵרָע וְשִׂפְתוֹתַי מִדַּבֵּר מִרְמָה, וְלִמְקַלְּלַי נַפְשִׁי תִדּוֹם, וְנַפְשִׁי כֶּעָפָר לַכֹּל תִּהְיֶה. פְּתַח לִבִּי בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ, וּבְמִצְוֹתֶיךָ תִּרְדּוֹף נַפְשִׁי. וְתַצִּילֵנִי מִפֶּגַע רָע, מִיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וּמֵאִשָּׁה רָעָה, וּמִכָּל רָעוֹת הַמִּתְרַגְּשׁוֹת לָבֹא בָּעוֹלָם. וְכָל הַחוֹשְׁבִים עָלַי רָעָה מְהֵרָה הָפֵר עֲצָתָם וְקַלְקֵל מַחְשְׁבוֹתָם. יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי לְפָנֶיךָ ה׳ צוּרִי וְגוֹאֲלִי״.
segments.en: «When Mar, son of Ravina, would conclude his prayer, he said the following:» «My God, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking deceit.» «To those who curse me let my soul be silent» «and may my soul be like dust to all.» «Open my heart to Your Torah,» «and may my soul pursue your mitzvot.» «And save me from a bad mishap, from the evil inclination,» «from a bad woman, and from all evils that suddenly come upon the world.» «And all who plan evil against me,» «swiftly thwart their counsel, and frustrate their plans.» «May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart find favor before You,» «Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer.»

segments.he: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת כִּי הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא, בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי: ״רִבּוֹן הָעוֹלָמִים, גָּלוּי לְפָנֶיךָ בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים, אָדָם חוֹטֵא — וּמַקְרִיב קָרְבָּן. וְאֵין מַקְרִיבִין מִמֶּנּוּ, אֶלָּא חֶלְבּוֹ וְדָמוֹ, וּמִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ. וְעַכְשָׁיו יָשַׁבְתִּי בְּתַעֲנִית וְנִתְמַעֵט חֶלְבִּי וְדָמִי, יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ שֶׁיְּהֵא חֶלְבִּי וְדָמִי שֶׁנִּתְמַעֵט כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרַבְתִּיו לְפָנֶיךָ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וְתִרְצֵנִי״.
segments.en: The Gemara recounts that «when Rav Sheshet would sit in» observance of «a fast, after he prayed he said as follows:» «Master of the Universe, it is revealed before You» that «when the Temple is standing, one sins and offers a sacrifice.» «And» although «only its fat and blood were offered from» that sacrifice on the altar, his transgression «is atoned for him.» «And now, I sat in» observance of «a fast and my fat and blood diminished.» «May it be Your will that my fat and blood that diminished be» considered as if «I offered» a sacrifice «before You on the altar,» «and may I find favor in Your eyes.» Having cited statements that various Sages would recite after their prayers, the Gemara cites additional passages recited by the Sages on different occasions.

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּי הֲוָה מְסַיֵּים סִפְרָא דְאִיּוֹב, אָמַר הָכִי: ״סוֹף אָדָם לָמוּת וְסוֹף בְּהֵמָה לִשְׁחִיטָה, וְהַכֹּל לְמִיתָה הֵם עוֹמְדִים. אַשְׁרֵי מִי שֶׁגָּדֵל בַּתּוֹרָה וַעֲמָלוֹ בַּתּוֹרָה, וְעוֹשֶׂה נַחַת רוּחַ לְיוֹצְרוֹ, וְגָדֵל בְּשֵׁם טוֹב וְנִפְטָר בְּשֵׁם טוֹב מִן הָעוֹלָם, וְעָלָיו אָמַר שְׁלֹמֹה: 'טוֹב שֵׁם מִשֶּׁמֶן טוֹב וְיוֹם הַמָּוֶת מִיּוֹם הִוָּלְדוֹ'״.
segments.en: «When Rabbi Yoḥanan would conclude» study of «the book of Job, he said the following:» «A person will ultimately die and an animal will ultimately be slaughtered, and all are destined for death.» Therefore, death itself is not a cause for great anguish. Rather, «happy is he who grew up in Torah, whose labor is in Torah,» «who gives pleasure to his Creator,» «who grew up with a good name and who took leave of the world with a good name.» Such a person lived his life fully, «and about him, Solomon said:» «“A good name is better than fine oil, and the day of death than the day of one’s birth”» (Ecclesiastes 7:1); one who was faultless in life reaches the day of his death on a higher level than he was at the outset.

segments.he: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר: ״גְּמוֹר בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכָל נַפְשְׁךָ לָדַעַת אֶת דְּרָכַי, וְלִשְׁקוֹד עַל דַּלְתֵי תוֹרָתִי. נְצוֹר תּוֹרָתִי בְּלִבְּךָ, וְנֶגֶד עֵינֶיךָ תִּהְיֶה יִרְאָתִי. שְׁמוֹר פִּיךְ מִכָּל חֵטְא, וְטַהֵר וְקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמְךָ מִכָּל אַשְׁמָה וְעָוֹן. וַאֲנִי אֶהְיֶה עִמְּךָ בְּכָל מָקוֹם״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Meir was wont to say» the following idiom: «Study with all your heart and with all your soul to know My ways» «and to be diligent at the doors of My Torah.» «Keep My Torah in your heart,» «and fear of Me should be before your eyes.» «Guard your mouth from all transgression,» «and purify and sanctify yourself from all fault and iniquity.» «And» if you do so, «I,» God, «will be with you everywhere.»

segments.he: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמַּיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּנַן דְּיַבְנֶה: ״אֲנִי בְּרִיָּה, וַחֲבֵרִי בְּרִיָּה. אֲנִי מְלַאכְתִּי בָּעִיר וְהוּא מְלַאכְתּוֹ בַּשָּׂדֶה. אֲנִי מַשְׁכִּים לִמְלַאכְתִּי, וְהוּא מַשְׁכִּים לִמְלַאכְתּוֹ. כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהוּא אֵינוֹ מִתְגַּדֵּר בִּמְלַאכְתִּי, כָּךְ אֲנִי אֵינִי מִתְגַּדֵּר בִּמְלַאכְתּוֹ. וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר: אֲנִי מַרְבֶּה, וְהוּא מַמְעִיט — שָׁנִינוּ: אֶחָד הַמַּרְבֶּה וְאֶחָד הַמַּמְעִיט וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּכַוֵּין לִבּוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם״.
segments.en: «The Sages in Yavne were wont to say:» «I» who learn Torah «am» God’s «creature and my counterpart» who engages in other labor «is» God’s «creature.» «My work is in the city and his work is in the field.» «I rise early for my work and he rises early for his work.» «And just as he does not presume to» perform «my work, so I do not presume to» perform «his work.» «Lest you say: I» engage in Torah study «a lot, while he» only engages in Torah study «a little,» so I am better than he, «it has» already «been taught:» «One who brings a substantial» sacrifice «and one who brings a meager» sacrifice have equal merit, «as long as he directs his heart towards Heaven» (Rav Hai Gaon, Arukh).

segments.he: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵּי: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם עָרוּם בְּיִרְאָה. ״מַעֲנֶה רַךְ מֵשִׁיב חֵמָה״. וּמַרְבֶּה שָׁלוֹם עִם אֶחָיו וְעִם קְרוֹבָיו וְעִם כָּל אָדָם וַאֲפִילּוּ עִם גּוֹי בַּשּׁוּק, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא אָהוּב לְמַעְלָה וְנֶחְמָד לְמַטָּה, וִיהֵא מְקוּבָּל עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת.
segments.en: «Abaye was wont to say:» «One must always be shrewd» and utilize every strategy «in» order to achieve «fear» of Heaven and performance of mitzvot. One must fulfill the verse: «“A soft answer turns away wrath”» (Proverbs 15:1) and take steps to «increase peace with one’s brethren and with one’s relatives,» «and with all people, even with a non-Jew in the marketplace,» despite the fact that he is of no importance to him and does not know him at all (Me’iri), «so that he will be loved above» in God’s eyes, «pleasant below» in the eyes of the people, «and acceptable to all» of God’s «creatures.»

segments.he: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי שֶׁלֹּא הִקְדִּימוֹ אָדָם שָׁלוֹם מֵעוֹלָם, וַאֲפִילּוּ גּוֹי בַּשּׁוּק.
segments.en: Tangentially, the Gemara mentions that «they said about Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai that no one ever preceded him in» issuing a «greeting, not even a non-Jew in the marketplace,» as Rabban Yoḥanan would always greet him first.

segments.he: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא: תַּכְלִית חָכְמָה — תְּשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא אָדָם קוֹרֵא וְשׁוֹנֶה וּבוֹעֵט בְּאָבִיו וּבְאִמּוֹ וּבְרַבּוֹ וּבְמִי שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ בְּחָכְמָה וּבְמִנְיָן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה יִרְאַת ה׳ שֵׂכֶל טוֹב לְכָל עוֹשֵׂיהֶם״. ״לָעוֹשִׂים״ לֹא נֶאֱמַר, אֶלָּא ״לְעוֹשֵׂיהֶם״ — לָעוֹשִׂים לִשְׁמָהּ וְלֹא לָעוֹשִׂים שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ. וְכָל הָעוֹשֶׂה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ, נוֹחַ לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא.
segments.en: «Rava was wont to say:» «The objective of» Torah «wisdom» is to achieve «repentance and good deeds;» «that one should not read» the Torah «and study» mishna and become arrogant «and spurn his father and his mother and his teacher» «and one who is greater than he in wisdom or in» the «number» of students who study before him, «as it is stated: “The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord, a good understanding have all who fulfill them”» (Psalms 111:10). «It is not stated» simply: «All who fulfill, but rather: All who fulfill them,» those who perform these actions as they ought to be performed, meaning «those who do» such deeds «for their own sake,» for the sake of the deeds themselves, «not those who do them not for their own sake.» Rava continued: «One who does them not for their own sake,» it would have been «preferable for him had he not been created.»

segments.he: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרַב: לֹא כָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא. הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵין בּוֹ לֹא אֲכִילָה וְלֹא שְׁתִיָּהּ וְלֹא פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה וְלֹא מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן וְלֹא קִנְאָה וְלֹא שִׂנְאָה וְלֹא תַּחֲרוּת, אֶלָּא צַדִּיקִים יוֹשְׁבִין וְעַטְרוֹתֵיהֶם בְּרָאשֵׁיהֶם וְנֶהֱנִים מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיֶּחֱזוּ אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים וַיֹּאכְלוּ וַיִּשְׁתּוּ״.
segments.en: «Rav was wont to say:» «The World-to-Come is not like this world.» «In the World-to-Come there is no eating, no drinking,» «no procreation, no» business «negotiations,» «no jealousy, no hatred, and no competition.» «Rather, the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads, enjoying the splendor of the Divine Presence, as it is stated:» «“And they beheld God, and they ate and drank”» (Exodus 24:11), meaning that beholding God’s countenance is tantamount to eating and drinking.

moves.cueHe: רבי אלעזר בתר דמסיים צלותיה אמר הכי
moves.summary: Rabbi Elazar's post-Amida petition for love, brotherhood, peace, disciples and a portion in Gan Eden
moves.about: petition that love, brotherhood, peace and friendship dwell in his lot and that his borders be rich in disciples

moves.cueHe: רבי יוחנן בתר דמסיים צלותיה אמר הכי
moves.summary: Rabbi Yoḥanan's petition that God look on Israel's shame and clothe Himself in mercy, might and grace
moves.about: petition that God look upon Israel's shame and clothe Himself in mercy, might, loving-kindness and grace

moves.cueHe: רבי זירא בתר דמסיים צלותיה אמר הכי
moves.summary: Rabbi Zeira's petition not to sin and not to be shamed before the forefathers
moves.about: petition not to sin and not to be shamed before the forefathers

moves.cueHe: רבי חייא בתר דמצלי אמר הכי
moves.summary: Rabbi Ḥiyya's petition that Torah be his vocation and his heart not grow faint
moves.about: petition that Torah be his vocation and that his heart not grow faint nor his eyes dim

moves.cueHe: רב בתר צלותיה אמר הכי
moves.summary: Rav's petition for a long life of peace, sustenance, dread of sin, wealth, honour and love of Torah
moves.about: petition for a long life of peace, goodness, blessing, sustenance, dread of sin, wealth, honor and love of Torah

moves.cueHe: רבי בתר צלותיה אמר הכי
moves.summary: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's petition for deliverance from arrogance, bad companions and harsh opponents
moves.about: petition for deliverance from arrogant men, a bad companion, a bad neighbour, the destructive Satan and a harsh opponent

moves.cueHe: ואף על גב דקיימי קצוצי עליה דרבי
moves.summary: the redactor notes that Rabbi said this daily even though royal officers guarded him
moves.about: that Rabbi recited this petition daily even though royal officers stood guard over him

moves.cueHe: רב ספרא בתר צלותיה אמר הכי
moves.summary: Rav Safra's petition for peace above and below and that Torah studied not for its own sake become study for its own sake; the prayer runs on into berakhot.17a.1
moves.about: petition for peace in the heavenly and earthly entourage and among students of Torah, and that those studying not for its own sake come to study for its own sake

moves.cueHe: רבי אלכסנדרי בתר צלותיה אמר הכי
moves.summary: Rabbi Alexandri's petition to be stationed in a lighted corner and not a darkened one
moves.about: petition to be stationed in a lighted corner and not a darkened one, and that his heart not grow faint nor his eyes dim

moves.cueHe: איכא דאמרי, הא רב המנונא מצלי לה
moves.summary: a variant tradition assigns that prayer to Rav Hamnuna instead
moves.about: what Rabbi Alexandri was in the habit of adding after his prayer

moves.cueHe: ורבי אלכסנדרי בתר דמצלי אמר הכי
moves.summary: on that variant, Rabbi Alexandri's own prayer is the one about the yeast in the dough and the subjugation to the kingdoms
moves.about: petition for deliverance from the yeast in the dough and the subjugation to the kingdoms, which alone prevent doing God's will

moves.cueHe: רבא בתר צלותיה אמר הכי
moves.summary: Rava's confession of unworthiness and plea to be cleansed by mercy and not by suffering
moves.about: confession of unworthiness and petition to sin no more and to be cleansed by mercy rather than by suffering and illness

moves.cueHe: והיינו וידוי דרב המנונא זוטי ביומא דכפורי
moves.summary: the redactor identifies Rava's petition with Rav Hamnuna Zuti's Yom Kippur confession
moves.about: what Rava was in the habit of adding after his prayer

moves.cueHe: מר בריה דרבינא כי הוה מסיים צלותיה אמר הכי
moves.summary: Mar son of Ravina's petition to be guarded from evil speech and from those who plan evil against him
moves.about: petition to be guarded from evil speech, from the evil inclination and from those who plan evil against him

moves.cueHe: רב ששת כי הוה יתיב בתעניתא, בתר דמצלי אמר הכי
moves.summary: Rav Sheshet's fast-day plea that his diminished fat and blood count as a sacrifice on the altar
moves.about: petition that the fat and blood diminished by his fast be reckoned as a sacrifice offered on the altar

moves.cueHe: רבי יוחנן כי הוה מסיים ספרא דאיוב, אמר הכי
moves.summary: opening the second series — sayings for other occasions: on finishing Job, that all are destined to die and only a good name endures
moves.about: adduces Solomon's verse that a good name is better than fine oil to seal the praise of one who dies with a good name

moves.cueHe: ועליו אמר שלמה
moves.summary: Ecclesiastes 7:1 is brought to seal the saying about a good name
moves.about: what Rabbi Yoḥanan would say whenever he completed the book of Job

moves.cueHe: מרגלא בפומיה דרבי מאיר
moves.summary: Rabbi Meir's habitual maxim: study wholeheartedly, guard your mouth, and God will be with you everywhere
moves.about: the maxim Rabbi Meir was habitually in the practice of repeating

moves.cueHe: מרגלא בפומייהו דרבנן דיבנה
moves.summary: the Sages of Yavne's habitual maxim: the city scholar and the field labourer are equally God's creatures, neither trespassing on the other's work
moves.about: adduces the taught ruling that one who brings much and one who brings little are equal provided the heart is directed to Heaven

moves.cueHe: ושמא תאמר: אני מרבה, והוא ממעיט
moves.summary: the anticipated claim that the one who studies more is the better man is floated, committing to nothing
moves.about: whether the one who studies much may claim superiority over the one who studies little — the anticipated claim is floated and then knocked down by the taught ruling

moves.cueHe: שנינו: אחד המרבה ואחד הממעיט
moves.summary: the floated claim is dismissed by the taught ruling that much and little are equal provided the heart is directed to Heaven

moves.cueHe: מרגלא בפומיה דאביי
moves.summary: Abaye's habitual maxim: be shrewd in fear of Heaven and increase peace with everyone, even a gentile in the marketplace
moves.about: quotes the verse 'a soft answer turns away wrath' as the conduct by which one increases peace

moves.cueHe: אמרו עליו על רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
moves.summary: a tradition attached to Abaye's maxim by the shared phrase 'even a gentile in the marketplace': no one ever greeted Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai first
moves.about: that no one, not even a gentile in the marketplace, ever greeted Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai first

moves.cueHe: מרגלא בפומיה דרבא
moves.summary: Rava's habitual maxim: the goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds, not learning that breeds contempt for one's elders
moves.about: adduces 'the beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord' as the prooftext that wisdom must issue in deeds

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ראשית חכמה יראת ה׳
moves.summary: Psalms 111:10 is adduced in support
moves.about: reads the suffix of לעושיהם as restricting the verse's praise to those who act for the deed's own sake

moves.cueHe: לעושים לא נאמר, אלא לעושיהם
moves.summary: the verse's suffix is expounded to restrict its praise to those who act for the deed's own sake
moves.about: the maxim Rava was habitually in the practice of repeating, that the goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds

moves.cueHe: מרגלא בפומיה דרב
moves.summary: Rav's habitual maxim: the World-to-Come has no eating, drinking or rivalry, only the righteous enjoying the radiance of the Divine Presence
moves.about: adduces 'and they beheld God, and they ate and drank' as proof that the righteous are sustained by the radiance of the Divine Presence

moves.cueHe: שנאמר: ויחזו את האלהים ויאכלו וישתו
moves.summary: Exodus 24:11 is adduced in support
moves.about: the maxim Rav was habitually in the practice of repeating, on the nature of the World-to-Come
